results.title: Visit Wolverhampton Art Gallery
highlights:
[Visit Wolverhampton Art Gallery > Getting here]

Buses 5, 6 and 876A from Stafford stop outside. Others stop at the university, including services from Cannock. The gallery is also a 5-minute walk from Wolverhampton’s busy bus station.

…

Trains run to Wolverhampton from: Sandwell & Dudley, Stafford, Birmingham New Street, Telford, Stoke-on-Trent and further afield. It’s then a 5-minute walk. On leaving the train station, cross the bridges and continue along Lichfield Street until you reach the gallery.

…

[Visit Wolverhampton Art Gallery > Accessibility]

- You can borrow noise cancelling headphones from the reception area.
- Please ask if you need a quiet space during your visit or if you need somewhere private to pray.
- There is level access throughout the building and lift access to all floors.
- We have a BSL Introduction to the Art Gallery and you can use the Convo App at our reception desk and pod for live BSL translation.
- We do not have a changing places toilet. The nearest changing place is at the Civic Centre during the week and Wolverhampton train station during the weekend.
- We have free wifi available.

highlights:
[West Midlands Museums & Galleries 2026: Ultimate Cultural Guide > Wolverhampton and Walsall’s Gallery Scene > Wolverhampton Art Gallery]

The permanent galleries also include a Georgian Room (with paintings by Gainsborough, Wright of Derby, and Edward Bird), a Victorian Room, and a diverse contemporary acquisitions programme. A regular Friday Lates programme extends opening beyond normal hours once a month for adult events, and the Glaze café on the ground floor has been recently refurbished. Admission is free. Open Monday to Saturday 10:30 am to 4:30 pm, Sunday 11 am to 4 pm. Address: Lichfield Street, Wolverhampton, WV1 1DU. The gallery is a five-minute walk from Wolverhampton train station, which has direct services from Birmingham New Street (approximately 20–25 minutes).
